question: Which Vedic God falls under the category of ‘Prithivisthana’(Terrestrial God)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihaspati**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Brihaspati, Agni, Soma, and Prithvi are all Vedic gods that fall under the category of “Prithivisthana” or Terrestrial Gods: 
 
• Brihaspati: Also known as Jupiter, Brihaspati is a benevolent god and part of the Hindu zodiac system.
 
• He is the heavenly prototype of the Brahmans and the earthly purohita, or family priest. 
 
• Agni: The chief god during the later Vedic period. 
 
• Soma: A god, plant, and ritual drink that was considered to bring health and wealth. 
 
• Prithvi: A terrestrial god. 
 
• In the Vedic Age, there were around 33 gods that were classified into three categories: Terrestrial, Aerial, and Celestial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vishnu, Indra, and Varuna are all deities in Hinduism and Vedic religion: 
 
• Vishnu
 
• The protector and preserver of the universe, Vishnu returns to Earth to restore balance between good and evil.
 
• Hindus believe he will be reincarnated one last time near the end of the world. 
 
• Indra
 
• Indra controls the universe and created rivers and streams by shaping mountains and valleys.
 
• He is often depicted with a thunderbolt and riding an elephant. Indra and Brahma are often shown giving the infant Buddha his first bath. 
 
• Varuna
 
• The first lord of the Cosmos, Varuna was usurped by Indra. In East Asian Buddhism, Varuna is a dharmapāla and is often called "Suiten" (water deva) in Japan. 
 
• Other deities in Vedic religion include:
 
• Agni, Dyaus, Rudra, Soma, Ashvinas, Mitra, Vayu, and Surya.
